processes: Pollination - moving pollen to the pistil
Attracting pollinators with color and scent
plainLanguageExplanation: A flower is the part of a plant that makes seeds. It has colorful petals that attract insects and birds, male parts called stamens that make a powder called pollen, and a female part called the pistil. Pollination is when pollen travels from one flower to the pistil of another flower. Once pollen lands on the pistil, fertilization can happen, and the flower's base swells into a fruit holding seeds. Each seed can grow into a new plant.

whyItMatters: Flowers are how many plants make the seeds that grow into the next generation. Understanding flowers explains how fruits form, how bees and birds feed, and why many plants depend on pollinators.
didYouKnow: A flower's colors and scents are signals to pollinators like bees, guiding them to the nectar so they help move pollen between flowers.
